sources.title: Ember / Our World in Data · Electricity demand
sources.detail: Annual demand, TWh. Includes grid losses and own-use as defined by Ember; derived from generation and net imports. Country and world series downloaded 14 September 2026.
sources.license: Ember CC BY 4.0; OWID CC BY

sources.title: IEA · Key Questions on Energy and AI (2026)
sources.detail: 2025 data-centre estimate: about 485 TWh. 2030 base case: about 950 TWh. AI-focused facilities approximately triple. Projections are scenarios, not commitments.

sources.title: IEA · Key Questions on Energy and AI, Figure 1.5
sources.detail: AI-focused data-centre electricity reaches about 465 TWh in the 2030 base case. Definition includes supporting infrastructure in AI-focused facilities.

sources.title: Our World in Data · How much energy do data centres and AI use?
sources.detail: 2025 AI-focused estimate of 155 TWh, based on IEA (2026). This is a facility-level proxy, not a workload-by-workload meter reading.

sources.title: Shanghai government · Power sustainability indicators, 2024
sources.detail: 198.4 TWh in 2024. Whole municipality; includes industry and surrounding districts, not just the urban core.

sources.title: Beijing government · Public utilities, 2024
sources.detail: 138.94 TWh in 2024. Electricity used across the Beijing municipality.

sources.title: Energy Market Authority · Singapore Energy Statistics
sources.detail: Approximately 58 TWh consumed in 2024. City-state final electricity consumption; different from Ember system demand.

sources.title: NYC Mayor’s Office of Climate · Energy systems
sources.detail: Approximately 50,000 GWh per year, citing NYISO (2024). Used as a rounded reference scale, not an exact annual observation.

sources.title: UK DESNZ · Regional electricity consumption, 2005–2024
sources.detail: 2024 workbook, London row, total consumption/all meters: 34,800.715594 GWh. Greater London; metered consumption excludes electricity self-consumed from on-site generation.

sources.title: Google · 2026 Environmental Report, page 93
sources.detail: Total operational electricity, 2021–2025, from the same restated series. 2025: 43,586,600 MWh; data centres: 42,415,800 MWh. Not an AI-only figure.

sources.title: Microsoft · 2026 Environmental Data Fact Sheet, Table 5
sources.detail: Electricity within the organization. FY2025: 37,026,353 MWh. Fiscal year ends 30 June. Includes cloud and other operations; AI share not separated.

sources.title: Meta · 2025 Environmental Data Index, page 6
sources.detail: 2024 total electricity: 18,423,634 MWh. Data centres: 18,061,781 MWh. Calendar-year company operations; includes social media and other workloads.

sources.title: TSMC · 2024 Sustainability Report, page 120
sources.detail: Approximate purchased electricity derived from 27,456 GWh total energy × 93.0% electricity = 25.5 TWh. Entire manufacturer, across all customers and chip applications; not AI-specific.

sources.title: Cambridge · Digital Mining Industry Report (April 2025)
sources.detail: 138 TWh annualised Bitcoin electricity estimate at the June 2024 reference point. A run rate, not a measured calendar-year total. Separate from the IEA data-centre boundary.

sources.title: Mytton et al. · Network energy use and the power model (2024)
sources.detail: Reports the IEA estimate of 260–360 TWh for global data-transmission networks in 2022. Covers all traffic, not just AI; traffic growth does not directly translate into proportional electricity growth.

sources.title: CSO Ireland · Data Centres Metered Electricity Consumption 2025
sources.detail: 2025: data centres 7.663 TWh out of 32.986 TWh metered electricity (23% rounded). Includes all data-centre workloads.

sources.title: Dwarkesh Podcast × Dylan Patel · 25 August 2026
sources.detail: Inspiration, not a measured energy dataset. At 00:00–07:01, the discussion extrapolates lab compute capacity at roughly 6 → 18 → 54 GW per lab at the end of 2026 → 2027 → 2028. Power boundary and utilization are not fully specified.

sources.title: OpenAI · Five new Stargate sites, September 2025
sources.detail: Nearly 7 GW of planned capacity across announced Stargate projects. Project scope overlaps with partner infrastructure; not current annual consumption.

sources.title: Anthropic · Compute partnership update, 6 May 2026
sources.detail: More than 300 MW of Colossus 1 capacity; up to 5 GW with Amazon; 5 GW with Google/Broadcom beginning in 2027. Agreements have different schedules and must not be added to provider electricity totals.
